title: Maximal associated prime criterion for flat local tensor extension
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of nonzero commutative local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, and assume that $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Assume that $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and that $B$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $M$ be any $A$-module. For a ring $T$ and $T$-module $P$, write $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ for the primes which are annihilators of elements of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. For an ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$, let $\mathfrak a B$ be the ideal generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak a)$. Give $M\otimes_A B$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] its $B$-module structure through the second factor and give $B/\mathfrak m_A B$ its quotient $B$-action. Then
$$\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\bigl(\mathfrak m_A\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)\ \text{and}\ \mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(B/\mathfrak m_A B)\bigr).$$
No Noetherianity of $B$ and no finite generation of $M$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres), local closed-point specialization with N=B, expanded through Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki) and the prime-quotient nonzerodivisor argument of Tag 05C1 (lemma-post-bourbaki).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-base-change] with $R=A$, $S=B$, $N=B$ and the given $M$. The flatness and Noetherian-base hypotheses hold; the theorem imposes neither finiteness on $M$ nor Noetherianity on $B$. The action through $N$ is precisely the stated $B$-action. Since $\mathfrak pN=\mathfrak pB$, its equality clause gives $\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)=\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)}\operatorname{Ass}_B(B/\mathfrak pB)$.

source.place: Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), equality clause; Tag 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres), closed-point case.

proof.text: Suppose $\mathfrak m_B$ belongs to the left side. Step 1 gives $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)$ and an element $0\ne z\in B/\mathfrak pB$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak m_B$, by [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. The witness is nonzero because $\operatorname{Ann}_B(0)=B$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ is proper. For $a\in\mathfrak p$, $\varphi(a)z=0$, hence $a\in\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 00LA (definition-associated); Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), contraction argument, specialized to the quotient witness.

proof.text: If $a\in\mathfrak m_A\setminus\mathfrak p$, multiplication by $a$ on $A/\mathfrak p$ is injective: $ar\in\mathfrak p$ implies $r\in\mathfrak p$ by primality. Tensor this injection with $B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Under [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring](1), the resulting injective map is multiplication by $\varphi(a)$ on $B/\mathfrak pB$: the quotient map sends $\bar r\otimes b$ to $\varphi(r)b\bmod\mathfrak pB$, and sends $a\bar r\otimes b$ to $\varphi(a)\varphi(r)b\bmod\mathfrak pB$. Here the $A$-submodule $\mathfrak pB$ is the extended ideal, since both consist of finite sums $\sum_i\varphi(p_i)b_i$. Locality gives $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$, contradicting this injectivity and $z\ne0$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$. Step 2 now supplies both required associations.

source.place: Tag 05C1 (lemma-post-bourbaki), proof: flatness makes nonzero scalars over the domain injective; Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), contraction paragraph. Quotient-tensor formula: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact).

proof.text: Conversely, if $\mathfrak m_A\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)$ and $\mathfrak m_B\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(B/\mathfrak m_AB)$, the summand indexed by $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ in the union of step 1 contains $\mathfrak m_B$. Its equality with $\operatorname{Ass}_B(M\otimes_A B)$ proves the reverse implication.

source.place: Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), inclusion clause; elementary membership in the union of step 1.

proof_origin.place: Local closed-point specialization of Tags 0312 (lemma-bourbaki) and 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres); the elementary contraction argument is written explicitly using the injectivity observation in Tag 05C1 (lemma-post-bourbaki).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q103-c02b0ac95 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the four nodes its proof cites and its stmt_deps in full, plus Stacks algebra.tex 15773-15900 (0312 lemma-bourbaki with its proof, 05C1, 05C2). Step 1: the 0312 node with R=A, S=B, N=B. Its hypotheses are only that N is R-flat and R is Noetherian, with no finiteness on M and no Noetherian condition on S, so the union formula holds; pN is the extended ideal pB. Step 2: an exact-annihilator witness z≠0 in B/pB gives p⊆φ⁻¹(m_B)=m_A, which is elementary. Step 3: for a in m_A\p, multiplication by a on A/p is injective because p is prime; it stays injective after tensoring with flat B (the 'in particular' clause of lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact); clause (1) of tensor-over-quotient-ring identifies the result with multiplication by φ(a) on B/pB, checked on pure tensors; φ(a)∈m_B=Ann(z) gives a contradiction, so p=m_A. Step 4: the m_A summand of the union. Edge cases checked: M=0; DVR with M=A and M=A/m; k→k[ε]/ε²; a non-Noetherian local B; flatness needed (k[t]_(t)→k); locality needed (k[t]_(t)→k(t), M=A). The statement matches its only citer, step 2 of the parent lem-trf-flat-pullback-associated-points. No duplicate: the fibre-bound node assumes B Noetherian and P finite, and the stalk-dictionary node is only the geometric translation. No SGA is cited.
